arxiv-2307-03837.title: Compactification of the energy surfaces for n n bodies
arxiv-2307-03837.creator: Andreas Knauf, Richard Montgomery
arxiv-2307-03837.description: Abstract For n n bodies moving in Euclidean d d –space under the influence of a homogeneous pair interaction we compactify every center of mass energy surface, obtaining a ( 2 ​ d ​ ( n − 1 ) − 1 ) (2d(n-1)-1) –dimensional manifold with corners in the sense of Melrose.

arxiv-2406-19803.title: Scalable and Domain-General Abstractive Proposition Segmentation
arxiv-2406-19803.creator: Mohammad Javad Hosseini, Yang Gao, Tim Baumgärtner, Alex Fabrikant, Reinald Kim Amplayo
arxiv-2406-19803.description: Abstract Segmenting text into fine-grained units of meaning is important to a wide range of NLP applications. The default approach of segmenting text into sentences is often insufficient, especially since sentences are usually complex enough to include multiple units of meaning that merit separate treatment in the downstream task.

arxiv-2508-12654.title: Symmetric power of higher dimensional varieties
arxiv-2508-12654.creator: Ashima Bansal, Supravat Sarkar, Shivam Vats
arxiv-2508-12654.description: Abstract . We study several properties of the symmetric power S m ​ X S^{m}X of a smooth variety X X . We describe the Picard and divisor class groups of S m ​ X S^{m}X when X X is projective.

arxiv-2510-04830.title: Anyon Bound States and Hybrid Superconductivity
arxiv-2510-04830.creator: Paul Leask
arxiv-2510-04830.description: Abstract The interactions of anyonic quasi-particles (vortices) in the Chern–Simons extension of the Ginzburg–Landau model is investigated and we show that it manifestly realizes a hybridization of type I/II superconductivity. Through Gauss’ law, each vortex simultaneously carries a flux quantum and a proportional Noether charge, thereby realizing an anyonic excitation.

pmc-10671719.title: Association between Decreased SGK1 and Increased Intestinal α-Synuclein in an MPTP Mouse Model of Parkinson’s Disease
pmc-10671719.creator: Min Hyung Seo, Dasom Kwon, Soo-Hwan Kim, Sujung Yeo, Maria Xilouri, Cristina Agliardi, Franca R Guerini
pmc-10671719.description: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a globally common progressive neurodegenerative disease resulting from the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the brain. Increased α-synuclein (α-syn) is associated with the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons and non-motor symptoms like gastrointestinal disorders. In this study, we investigated the association between serum/glucocorticoid-related kinase 1 (SGK1) and α-syn in the colon of a PD mouse model.

pmc-10730979.title: Exploration of the biomarkers of comorbidity of psoriasis with inflammatory bowel disease and their association with immune infiltration
pmc-10730979.creator: Rui‐Lian Ding, Yu Zheng, Jin Bu
pmc-10730979.description: BackgroundThere was evidence that significant bidirectional associations between psoriasis and inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs), which influences management strategy of the patients, so the investigation on the mechanisms by which these two diseases co‐occur is important.MethodsThe Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database was used to download gene expression profiles of psoriasis and IBD.

pmc-11535760.title: Cross-disciplinary working between gynaecologists and mental healthcare professionals: a mixed-methods systematic review protocol
pmc-11535760.creator: Yvonne Hartnett, Rebecca Conlan-Trant, Richard Duffy, Anne M Doherty
pmc-11535760.description: AbstractIntroductionReproductive hormone transitions (menstrual cycle, post partum and menopause) can trigger mental disorders in a subset of women. Gynaecological diseases, such as endometriosis and polycystic ovary syndrome, can also elevate the risk of mental illness. The link between psychiatrists and obstetricians is already well established in the peripartum period; however, the link between gynaecology and psychiatry is less so.

pmc-12377705.title: Strength training promotes attenuation of fatty liver while improving insulin resistance and inflammatory biomarkers in obese rats induced by high-fat diet
pmc-12377705.creator: S. Torezani-Sales, A.P.L. Damiani, A.R. Madureira, J.P. Cordeiro, G.H. Taufner, B.V. Nogueira, M.C. Dias, M.M. Sugizaki, A.S. Leopoldo, A.P. Lima-Leopoldo
pmc-12377705.description: Obesity is an independent risk factor for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Non-pharmacological strategies, such as strength training (ST), have been investigated for their effectiveness in attenuating MASLD. This study evaluated the effects of ST on hepatic fat accumulation in an experimental model of obesity.

pmc-12722246.title: Daily steps are a predictor of, but perhaps not a risk factor for Parkinson’s disease: findings from the UK Biobank
pmc-12722246.creator: Aidan Acquah, Andrew Creagh, Valentin Hamy, Alaina Shreves, Charilaos Zisou, Charlie Harper, Stefan van Duijvenboden, Chrystalina Antoniades, Derrick Bennett, David Clifton, Aiden Doherty
pmc-12722246.description: Previous studies link lower physical activity with incident Parkinson’s disease (PD) but rely on self-reported data and fail to address reverse causation. This study used accelerometer-derived daily step count, an objective measure of physical activity, to examine its association with incident PD in the UK Biobank, within successive periods of follow-up.

pmc-12853830.title: Impact of precipitation patterns on the risk of hand, foot, and mouth disease in Southwest China: insight from a disease burden perspective
pmc-12853830.creator: Jun-Yan Xi, Jie Sun, Jing Gu, Yuan-Tao Hao, Xiao Lin
pmc-12853830.description: BackgroundPrecipitation is regarded as a pivotal upstream factor in the control of the hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) burden. However, the current evidence on the direction and magnitude of precipitation patterns on HFMD burden remains unclear.MethodsWe conducted a population-based ecological time-series study using daily HFMD cases and meteorological data from 88 counties in Guizhou, China, between 2012 and 2019.

pmc-13150213.title: Peri-implant soft tissue response to different abutment materials: A randomised controlled clinical trial
pmc-13150213.creator: Sarvesh Ingole, Sukhada Pawar, Sowjanya Gunukula, Akshay J Melath, Zameer Pasha, Nishant Visvas Dumont, Krutika Bidkar
pmc-13150213.description: Peri-implant soft tissue response varies with different transmucosal abutment materials, but their comparative effects on clinical, histologic and microbiologic markers are not well understood. This randomized, controlled, split-mouth clinical trial compared titanium (Ti), zirconia (Zr) and titanium with a TiO2 bioactive coating (Ti+TiO2) in 50 systemically healthy participants.

pmc-13597326.creator: Ke Liu, Junxiang Zhang, Yaru Ren, Haochen Wang, Shuting Yang, Ziyang Xue, Yanjun Sun, Ting Liang, Xuqi Li, Shufeng Wang
pmc-13597326.description: IntroductionPreoperative distinction between well-differentiated liposarcoma (WDLPS) and dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS) remains difficult on conventional imaging. We evaluated whether CT attenuation-defined regional radiomics provides additional discriminatory information beyond whole-tumor radiomics and simple quantitative CT measurements.MethodsThis retrospective study included 97 patients with surgically confirmed retroperitoneal liposarcoma (57 WDLPS and 40 DDLPS) who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced CT.
